plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a cash buffer. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to small positions to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.

This plan balances growth potential with a focus on risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new, high-quality long setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Add to all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to 6% each, leaning into higher-risk, higher-reward positions.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy COP at 6% as a new, high-scoring long setup from the scanner.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero to reduce risk.
Add to QQQI to 30% to increase income exposure.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
It shifts the portfolio towards income-generating assets.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It minimizes high-beta and leveraged positions to prioritize low drawdown and reliable income. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff.
